key_insight: A lightweight machine-learning interatomic potential trained on unary and binary systems transfers to unseen ternary and quaternary alloys by interpolating learned interactions.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a route to reusable, resource-efficient alloy simulations without developing a custom potential for every composition.
method: Use step-wise active learning to build a compact, diverse training dataset.
Train a general-purpose potential spanning Al, Sc, Ti, V, Cu, Zn, Zr, Nb, Mo, Hf, Ta and W.
Extend to new elements through alchemical extrapolation using only unary data for each new element.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports transfer from unary and binary training data to ternary and quaternary systems, plus transfer to new elements and their alloys, but provides no numerical accuracy or runtime results.
watch_item: Validate accuracy for target compositions and operating conditions before deployment; the abstract does not establish transferability across all alloy environments.
paper_title: Learning Between the Lines: Interaction Interpolation in a Multi Element Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
